name: NASA_DONKI_get_coronal_mass_ejections
description: Search NASA DONKI (Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information) for Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) events. Returns CME observations including start time, source location, active region, speed, direction, half-angle, and linked geomagnetic storms. No API key required. Date range defaults to last 30 days if not specified. Essential for space weather research, satellite operations planning, and aurora forecasting.

startDate.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., '2024-01-01'). Defaults to 30 days before endDate.

endDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., '2024-01-31'). Defaults to today.

startTime.description: CME start time in ISO format

cmeAnalyses.description: CME measurements including speed, direction, half-angle

type.description: CME type (S=Slow, C=Common, O=Occasional, R=Rare, ER=Extremely Rare)

enlilList.description: ENLIL model runs for the event, each with its completion time and predicted arrival. Measured on 18 of 40 analyses - the actual forecast, as distinct from the observation.

featureCode.description: Which feature was tracked, e.g. 'LE' for leading edge. Speeds measured on different features differ systematically.

imageType.description: The image product measured, e.g. 'running difference'.

levelOfData.description: Data level, e.g. 0 for real-time and higher for reprocessed. A level-0 speed is provisional.

link.description: The event's page in DONKI, e.g. 'https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/view/CME/28...'.

measurementTechnique.description: How the CME was measured, e.g. 'Plane-of-sky'. A plane-of-sky speed is a projection and so a LOWER BOUND on the true speed; a 3D fit is not. Reading the two alike understates fast Earth-directed events.

note.description: Why the analysis is limited, e.g. '3D measurement not possible because the source...'. Present on all 40 measured analyses, and it is what explains a plane-of-sky-only figure.

speedMeasuredAtHeight.description: Solar radii at which the speed was measured, e.g. 16.7. Measured on 35 of 40 analyses. CMEs accelerate, so a speed without its height is not comparable.

submissionTime.description: When the record was submitted, e.g. '2025-02-06T17:44Z' - over a year after the event. The analysis is often revised long afterwards.

time21_5.description: When the CME reached 21.5 solar radii, e.g. '2024-01-02T01:01Z'. The standard reference surface for arrival-time models.

catalog.description: Which DONKI catalog the event is from, e.g. 'M2M_CATALOG'. Catalogs use different measurement conventions, so speeds are not comparable across them.

link.description: The event's page in DONKI, e.g. 'https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/view/CME/28...'.

sentNotifications.description: Space-weather notifications issued for the event, each with its messageID. Measured on 5 of 36 events. Whether anyone was actually warned.

submissionTime.description: When the record was submitted, e.g. '2025-02-06T17:44Z' - over a year after the event. The analysis is often revised long afterwards.

versionId.description: Which revision of the record this is, e.g. 2. An earlier version may have reported a different speed.

name: NASA_DONKI_get_solar_flares
description: Search NASA DONKI for Solar Flare (FLR) events. Returns flare observations including class (C/M/X), begin/peak/end times, source location, and active region. Solar flares are classified by X-ray peak brightness: C-class (small), M-class (medium, can cause brief radio blackouts), X-class (major, can cause global radio blackouts). No API key required.

name: NASA_DONKI_get_geomagnetic_storms
description: Search NASA DONKI for Geomagnetic Storm (GST) events. Returns storm observations including Kp index values (measure of geomagnetic disturbance: 5=minor storm, 6=moderate, 7=strong, 8=severe, 9=extreme). Geomagnetic storms can cause aurora displays, GPS disruptions, power grid problems, and satellite drag. No API key required.

startDate.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., '2024-01-01'). Defaults to 30 days before endDate.

endDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., '2024-06-30'). Defaults to today.

name: NASA_DONKI_get_solar_energetic_particles
description: Search NASA DONKI for Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) events. SEPs are high-energy particles (protons, electrons, heavy ions) accelerated by solar flares and CME-driven shocks. They pose radiation hazards to astronauts, satellites, and high-altitude aircraft. Returns event time, associated instruments, and linked solar events. No API key required.

name: NASA_DONKI_get_interplanetary_shocks
description: Search NASA DONKI for Interplanetary Shock (IPS) events detected at Earth or in the solar wind. Interplanetary shocks are sudden increases in solar wind speed, density, and magnetic field strength, often driven by CMEs or stream interaction regions. They can trigger geomagnetic storms. Returns event time, location, detecting instruments, and linked events. No API key required.

endDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., '2024-03-31'). Defaults to today.

location.description: Shock detection location. Options: 'Earth', 'STEREO A', 'STEREO B', 'MESSENGER', 'Mars'. Default: all locations.

link.description: The event's page in DONKI, e.g. 'https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/view/CME/28...'.

name: NASA_DONKI_get_high_speed_streams
description: Search NASA DONKI for High Speed Stream (HSS) events in the solar wind. HSSs originate from coronal holes on the Sun and can cause minor to moderate geomagnetic storming when they interact with Earth's magnetosphere. They produce recurrent geomagnetic activity patterns (27-day cycle) and are a major source of space weather disturbances during solar minimum. No API key required.

endDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., '2024-06-30'). Defaults to today.
